events.what: Chan proves there are no three consecutive powerful numbers whose middle term is a perfect cube and whose outer terms each have a single prime factor to an odd power (INTEGERS 25 (2025) #A7)
She rules out a further family of consecutive powerful triples centred on cubes with prime-square factors
van Doorn on three-term arithmetic progressions of powerful numbers; bears on Erdős #938, not on this bullet
events.ai_basis: ChatGPT was used as a sounding board, for proofreading and for supplying numerical examples ... The paper itself was entirely human-generated.

events.what: Ma generalises Chan's cube-centred result to middle terms that are certain other perfect powers

judgement.doubts: I agree with the record's codes. The cases are infinite structural families (a class of objects), not finite instances, so the scope is 'case'. INTEGERS received Chan's paper on 17 Oct 2024, but the first public written argument the record shows is the arXiv post of 27 Mar 2025; either date is after the snapshot. The ai.basis_quote comes from van Doorn's paper (a variant, not counted), not from the event the status rests on. It is left in place, and the AI role is 'none' either way.
